extracted.intended_audience: attorneys practicing before the USPTO; respondents in USPTO OED disciplinary/probation proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Conditions and procedural requirements imposed on an attorney placed on probation by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED), including education, attestations, monitoring, reporting, cooperation, and enforcement steps for non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: hours of continuing legal education as follows: two (2) hours on ethics/professional responsibility and four (4) hours on U.S. trademark law;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These CLE hours are required as part of the probationary conditions (timing implied: during the probationary period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit verifying review of trademark guidance and rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the conclusion of the probationary period, Respondent shall provide to the OED Director a sworn affidavit or verified declaration attesting that Respondent has reviewed thoroughly (i) all provisions of the Trademark Manual of Examining Procedure ("TMEP"), including, but not limited to, the provisions the USPTO's signature requirements, (ii) 37 C.F.R. § 2.11, and (iii) the commentary on the Requirement of U.S. Licensed Attorney for Foreign Trademark Applicants and Registrants, found at 84 FR 31498 (July 2, 2019);
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavit/verified declaration must be submitted to the OED Director prior to the end of probation and must attest to thorough review of the listed materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weekly USPTO TESS searches and prompt notification
rubrics_metrics.description: On at least a weekly basis throughout the term of the probationary period, Respondent shall (i) search the USPTO Trademark Electronic Search System ("TESS") for applications identifying him as the attorney of record and (ii) promptly inform appropriate personnel at the USPTO in writing of any filings identifying him as the attorney of record that were not made by him or with his knowledge and consent;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Searches must be conducted at least weekly for applications naming the respondent as attorney of record; any unauthorized or unknown filings discovered must be promptly reported in writing to appropriate USPTO personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly reporting of TESS search completion
rubrics_metrics.description: On a quarterly basis throughout the term of the probationary period, Respondent shall submit a written report to the OED Director stating that he has completed the searches of the USPTO TESS database required by section g., above, and, if applicable, stating that he identified no applications in which he was named as the attorney of record that were not made by him or made without his knowledge and consent;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly written reports must confirm completion of the required searches and either report any unauthorized listings or affirm none were found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cooperation with USPTO inquiries into impermissible signings or improper filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall cooperate fully with the USPTO in any present or future USPTO inquiry made into other impermissible signings or other improper filings of trademark documents filed with the USPTO by trademark agencies with whom Respondent works or had worked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full cooperation with USPTO investigations (past or future) concerning impermissible signings or improper filings by associated trademark agencies is required for the duration specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement: Order to Show Cause and potential suspension for non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) If the OED Director is of the opinion that Respondent, during his probationary period, failed to comply with any provision of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct; the provisions of the Proposed Settlement Agreement; the Final Order; or any of the above conditions identified in items c. though e., the OED Director shall: (A) issue to Respondent an Order to Show Cause why the USPTO Director should not enter an order immediately suspending the Respondent for up to twelve (12) months for the violations set forth in the Joint Legal Conclusions, above; (B) send the Order to Show Cause to Respondent at [address]; (C) grant Respondent fifteen (15) days to respond to the Order to Show Cause;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance may trigger formal enforcement: issuance and service of an Order to Show Cause, a 15-day response period, and possible immediate suspension up to 12 months based on the Joint Legal Conclusions. The OED Director initiates this procedure upon belief of non-compliance.
